tweet.text:
Speculative decoding is quietly becoming one of the biggest battlegrounds in LLM inference.

llama.cpp just shipped v0.6.0 with MTP speculative decoding for Qwen4Exp, reporting ~1.5× decode speedup on DGX Spark.

And vLLM is going in a different direction with EAGLE, DFlash and DSpark.

The interesting part isn’t “which engine is faster?”

It’s this:

How much of the model’s next-token computation can we predict before the target model has to do it?

Traditional speculative decoding:
→ Draft model proposes tokens
→ Target model verifies them

MTP:
→ The model itself provides future-token predictions

EAGLE:
→ A lightweight learned predictor works from the target model’s internal representations

Same goal. Very different trade-offs.

And this is why I think inference engineering is becoming less about:

“Run the model faster.”

and more about:

“Avoid doing unnecessary computation in the first place.”

The next 2–3 years of inference optimization are going to be fascinating.
